gate.title: Admins only
gate.description: Settings — instance configuration, taxonomy management and the role overview — is available to administrators. Ask an admin if you need a change here.

hub.title: Settings
hub.subtitle: Instance configuration, taxonomy management, roles and service accounts — administrators only.

taxonomies.title: Taxonomies
taxonomies.description: Manage the categories that classify assets, applications, consumables and knowledge-base articles — plus asset models.

locations.title: Locations
locations.description: Manage the places your assets physically live — offices, datacenters, racks and storage.

imports.title: Bulk import
imports.description: Load an existing estate of assets from a CSV or JSON file — a guided, occasional admin action for a new instance.

roles.title: Roles
roles.description: See who has which RBAC role across the team. Role changes happen in the Users section.

serviceAccounts.title: Service accounts
serviceAccounts.description: Create and manage non-human API credentials for CI, scripts and integrations — scoped by permission and revocable.

agents.title: Reporting agents
agents.description: Set how every lazyit agent in this estate reports and what it collects, and review which discovered hosts are confirmed automatically.

integrations.title: Integrations & workflows
integrations.description: The cross-application manual-task inbox for provisioning workflows. Per-app automation is configured on each application's Workflows tab.

instance.title: Instance
instance.description: Review how this lazyit instance is configured — identity provider, setup state and runtime posture.

instance.title: Instance
instance.subtitle: How this lazyit instance is configured — runtime posture (set via environment) and the asset-tag scheme.
instance.loadErrorHint: The API may be down or unreachable.

agentsMoved.title: Reporting agents
agentsMoved.body: The fleet's agent policy — reporting cadence, collectors and exclusions — now has its own section, together with the auto-confirm rules and the scopes that can override it.

updates.title: Version & updates
updates.subtitle: Check for new lazyit releases and run a guided, backed-up update from the host.

state.behind: {count, plural, one {# version behind} other {# versions behind}}
state.securityBehind: {count, plural, one {# version behind — security} other {# versions behind — security}}

security.title: Security update available
security.description: A release in this gap addresses security-relevant issues. Updating promptly is recommended.

optIn.label: Check for updates weekly
optIn.description: Anonymously check github.com for new releases. Off by default; no instance data is ever sent, and it fails silently if blocked.
optIn.smtpHint: To also get emailed when you fall behind, configure SMTP in the card below.

cta.hint: This records the update and shows the exact command to run on the host — nothing runs automatically.

command.instruction: Run this on the host to apply the update. It backs up both databases (verified) before anything, and won't proceed if the backup fails:
command.reconnecting: Update in progress — the app may be briefly unreachable while it restarts. This page reconnects automatically.

runStatus.requested: Update requested — run the command below on the host

toast.enqueued: Update queued. Run the shown command on the host to apply it.

cancel.hint: Haven't run the command yet? Cancel to clear this request and check for updates again later.
cancel.toast: Update cancelled. You can check for updates again anytime.

assetTagScheme.title: Asset tag scheme
assetTagScheme.subtitle: Auto-assign a running asset tag to new assets — a prefix, a zero-padded number and a suffix. Off until you turn it on; an explicit tag always wins.
assetTagScheme.loadError: Could not load the asset-tag scheme.
assetTagScheme.disabledHint: The scheme is off. New assets keep their manual tag (or none) — turn it on to auto-assign.

preview.label: Next tag
preview.digits: {count, plural, =0 {a number} one {# digit} other {# digits}}
preview.skipped: Skipped {count, plural, one {# number that is already in use} other {# numbers that are already in use}}, starting at {from}.

enabled.label: Auto-assign asset tags
enabled.description: When on, a new asset with no tag gets the next number automatically.

width.label: Number width
width.description: Zero-pad the number to this many digits (e.g. 4 → 0042). Leave blank for no padding.

startNumber.label: Start at
startNumber.description: Optional. Re-seed the counter so the next tag starts here. Leave blank to continue the sequence.

toast.saveError: Could not save the asset-tag scheme.

seedSuggestion.message: {count, plural, one {# existing tag matches} other {# existing tags match}} this pattern (highest: {highest}). Suggested start: {start}.

backfill.title: Tag existing assets
backfill.subtitle: Apply the scheme to assets that already exist. Review the proposed tags below, deselect any you want to skip, then apply. This writes new tags and is audited — there is no bulk undo.

mode.label: What to tag
mode.untaggedOnlyHint: Only assets that have no tag yet will get one. Existing tags are left untouched.
mode.normalizeHint: Also re-tag assets whose tag doesn't match this scheme. Conforming tags are never changed.

warning.title: This overwrites existing tags
warning.body: Non-conforming mode replaces tags that someone set by hand — which may be printed on physical labels. The change is audited but cannot be bulk-undone. Conforming tags are never touched.

backfill.empty: No assets match this scope — nothing to tag.
backfill.apply: Tag {count, plural, one {# asset} other {# assets}}

agentPolicy.title: Reporting agents
agentPolicy.subtitle: The default policy for every lazyit agent in this estate — how often they report, what they collect and what they leave out. Set here once, with no host to log into.
agentPolicy.loadFailed: Could not load the agent policy.
agentPolicy.saveFailed: Could not save the agent policy.
agentPolicy.saved: Saved as policy v{revision}. Agents apply it on their next report.

conflict.body: This policy was saved from somewhere else while you were editing — it is now v{revision}. Your changes are still here and have not been sent. Save to replace v{revision} with them, or reload to start from it and lose what you typed.

agentPolicy.propagation: A change takes effect on each host's next check-in, then applies from the run after that. That short delay is deliberate: a policy is only ever applied by a run that started with it already in place, so a mistake here can never interrupt a fleet mid-collection.

cadence.title: Cadence
cadence.description: How often a host reports, and how long lazyit waits before calling it offline. The two are tied together: the offline threshold has to be longer than the interval, or a healthy host is marked offline between two of its own reports.

interval.label: Report every (minutes)
interval.help: How often each host reports. The scheduler on the host ticks every {tick} minutes and does nothing on a tick inside this interval, so changing this never touches a host's timer.
interval.invalid: Enter a whole number of minutes between {min} and {max}.

stale.label: Consider a host offline after (minutes)
stale.help: How long lazyit waits after a host's last report before marking it offline on the map and raising a notification.
stale.invalid: Enter a whole number of minutes between {min} and {max}.
stale.belowInterval: This must be longer than the reporting interval, or a healthy host is marked offline between two of its own reports.

softwareMax.label: Maximum packages per host
softwareMax.help: A hard cap on the installed-software list. Lower it on hosts whose package list is more noise than inventory.
softwareMax.invalid: Enter a whole number between 0 and {max}.
softwareMax.inert: Installed software is off above, so this cap changes nothing until you turn it back on.

collect.title: What agents collect
collect.description: On Linux a collector that is off is never run — the agent does not gather the facts and then discard them. On Windows only containers works that way: hardware, disks, network interfaces and installed software all ride one PowerShell call that runs either way, so switching one off there keeps the fact out of the report but does not save the host the work.
collect.veto: A host can always refuse. Turning a collector off in that host's own agent config — /etc/lazyit-agent/config on Linux, C:\ProgramData\lazyit-agent\config on Windows — wins over this setting, and nothing here can switch it back on.

exclude.title: Exclusions
exclude.description: Comma-separated name patterns; the whole name has to match, and matching is case-insensitive. * stands for any run of characters, ? for exactly one — regular expressions are not accepted. Each list holds at most {max} patterns.

nicNames.label: Ignore network interfaces
nicNames.help: Interfaces whose name matches are left out of the report.
nicNames.inert: Network interfaces are off above, so this list changes nothing until you turn them back on.

mountpoints.label: Ignore mountpoints
mountpoints.help: Disks mounted here are left out of the report. Unmounted disks are never affected.
mountpoints.inert: Disks and mountpoints are off above, so this list changes nothing until you turn them back on.

softwareNames.label: Ignore packages
softwareNames.help: Package name patterns to leave out — kernel builds are the usual case.
softwareNames.inert: Installed software is off above, so this list changes nothing until you turn it back on.

globs.invalid: “{value}” is not a valid pattern. Use letters, digits, - _ / : and the * and ? wildcards — regular expressions are not accepted.

scopes.title: Where a policy comes from
scopes.description: Three scopes, resolved field by field — the narrowest one that sets a field wins.

serviceAccount.label: Per service account
serviceAccount.scope: One agent's credential — the Add a server wizard mints one per agent.

scopes.footer: The API stores all three scopes, but no screen in lazyit writes the narrower two. So this page is what a host runs — unless one of the other two was set through the API directly, or the host's own agent config vetoes part of it. A local setting can only ever make a host report less than this page asks, never more: a longer interval, a lower package cap, extra exclusions, a collector switched off. Nothing here overrides one.

rollout.title: Rollout
rollout.body: Each host echoes the policy version it is actually running, so “configured” and “applied” stay different things. A host picks a change up on its next check-in and applies it from the run after that.
rollout.legacy: A server discovered by an agent older than this channel never echoes a version at all, and shows neither applied nor pending.
rollout.link: See per-host status on the infrastructure diagram

autoConfirm.title: Auto-confirm rules
autoConfirm.description: Which discovered hosts are confirmed the moment they report instead of waiting in Pending review. A rule only ever applies to reports that arrive after you save it.
autoConfirm.summary: {total, plural, one {# rule} other {# rules}}, {enabled} enabled
autoConfirm.empty: No rules — every discovered host waits in Pending review.

smtp.title: Outbound email (SMTP)
smtp.subtitle: Connect an SMTP relay so lazyit can send email notifications. Off until you turn it on; the password is stored encrypted and never shown again.
smtp.loadError: Could not load the SMTP settings.
smtp.loadErrorHint: Check your connection and try again.
smtp.disabledHint: Outbound email is off. Turn it on to email notifications — you can still send a test below.

enabled.label: Enable outbound email
enabled.description: When on, eligible notifications are also emailed. When off, nothing is emailed (you can still send a test).

password.label: Password
password.hintSet: A password is stored. Leave blank to keep it, or type a new one to replace it.

rejectUnauthorized.label: Verify TLS certificate
rejectUnauthorized.description: Reject relays whose TLS certificate can't be verified. Turn off only to allow a self-signed certificate on a trusted relay.

test.heading: Send a test email
test.description: Sends a one-off email using the saved settings. Save your changes first — the test uses what's stored, not the form above.
test.invalidEmail: Enter a valid destination email address.
test.failure: The test email could not be sent.
test.error: Could not send the test email.

toast.saveError: Could not save the SMTP settings.

directory.title: AD / LDAP directory sync
directory.subtitle: Read-only import of people from your on-prem Active Directory / LDAP. lazyit creates login-less directory persons — it never writes back to your directory and never logs anyone in.
directory.loadError: Could not load the directory settings.
directory.loadErrorHint: Check your connection and try again.
directory.disabledHint: Scheduled sync is off. Turn it on to import people on a schedule — you can still run Sync now below to test the connection.

enabled.label: Enable scheduled sync
enabled.description: When on, lazyit periodically binds to your directory and imports people. When off, only a manual Sync now runs.

hint.ldaps: Encrypted from the first byte. The recommended default.
hint.starttls: Connects in plaintext, then upgrades to TLS.
hint.plaintext: Unencrypted — the bind password travels in the clear. Only for a trusted internal segment.

rejectUnauthorized.label: Verify TLS certificate
rejectUnauthorized.description: Reject a directory whose TLS certificate can't be verified. Turn off only to allow a self-signed certificate on a trusted internal server.
rejectUnauthorized.plaintextHint: Not applicable to a plaintext connection (there is no TLS to verify).

baseDN.label: Search base (base DN)
baseDN.description: The subtree lazyit searches for people.

bindDN.label: Bind DN
bindDN.description: The read-only service account lazyit binds as. This identifies the credential; it is not itself the secret.

bindPassword.label: Bind password
bindPassword.hintSet: A bind password is stored. Leave blank to keep it, or type a new one to replace it.

searchFilter.label: Search filter
searchFilter.description: The LDAP filter selecting which entries to import. Run verbatim — there is no per-user substitution.

offboardGraceDays.label: Offboard grace (days)
offboardGraceDays.description: How many days a person may be missing from the directory before lazyit deactivates them. 0 = deactivate on the first sync that no longer finds them.

attributeMap.label: Attribute mapping
attributeMap.description: Which directory attribute fills each lazyit field. Leave a field blank to skip it.

sync.heading: Sync now
sync.description: Runs the same read-only import the schedule runs, using the saved settings — so save your changes first. This also confirms the bind works.
sync.error: Could not run the directory sync.

tray.title: Directory people to review
tray.description: People imported from your directory. Each is a login-less person you can open, provision a login for, or offboard from the Users section.

toast.saveError: Could not save the directory settings.

roles.title: Roles
roles.subtitle: Who holds which access level, and what each role can do. Change a role from the Users section.
roles.viewMembers: View {count, plural, =0 {no members} one {# member} other {# members}}

ADMIN.label: Admin
ADMIN.hint: Full access, including user administration and destructive deletes.

MEMBER.label: Member
MEMBER.hint: Normal inventory, KB and asset operations.

permissions.title: Role permissions
permissions.subtitle: Configure what Members and Viewers can do. Admin always has full access.
permissions.idpNote: These permissions are lazyit-only — they never appear in your identity provider.

segmented.adminTitle: Admin has full access and cannot be edited.

preset.customHint: A one-off set that matches no preset.

fineTune.title: Fine-tune (advanced)
fineTune.subtitle: Exact per-permission control
fineTune.description: Each switch here is a single permission. Changes flip the role to a Custom set and update the capability toggles above.

confirm.title: Review this change before saving
confirm.description: This update has effects worth confirming. Review them, then save.

consequence.removedRead: {who} will no longer be able to {action}.
consequence.accessGrantGrant: {who} will be able to grant and revoke application access for anyone — including to sensitive applications. This is normally an admin-only action.
consequence.userManage: {who} will be able to administer users: create accounts, change roles (including granting ADMIN) and offboard people. This is normally an admin-only action.
consequence.settingsManage: {who} will be able to configure the instance and manage taxonomies — the full admin configuration surface. This is normally an admin-only action.
consequence.deleteDefault: {who} will be able to {action} — a destructive action normally reserved for admins.

serviceAccounts.title: Service accounts
serviceAccounts.subtitle: Non-human API credentials for CI, scripts and integrations — scoped by permission, never a role.

systemManaged.hint: Owned by the workflow engine — every workflow run executes as this account.
systemManaged.locked: System-managed — the workflow engine runs as this account, so it can't be edited, rotated or revoked.

empty.title: No service accounts yet
empty.revokedDescription: Revoked (soft-deleted) accounts appear here and can be restored.
empty.description: Give a CI runner, script or integration scoped, non-human access to the API — create one and hand it a token instead of a person's login.

serviceAccounts.revokeExplanation: Its token stops authenticating immediately. You can restore it from the “Show revoked” view (rotate to mint a fresh token). Revoking suspends the token but does not remove vault access — use the vault's Members list to revoke per vault and remove key material.

toast.copyUnavailable: Copy isn't available here (it needs HTTPS) — use Download or select the token and copy it manually.

form.editDescription: Update the name, permissions and lifecycle of this non-human credential. The token is not changed here — use Rotate for that.
form.newDescription: A non-human credential (a CI runner, a script, an integration). It is authorized by the permissions you grant — never a role. The token is shown once after you create it.
form.descriptionPlaceholder: Optional — what this credential is used for.
form.expiresHint: Optional. After this time the token is rejected. Leave empty for no expiry.
form.activeHint: A soft disable. When off, the token stops authenticating without revoking the account.
form.permissionsHint: The capabilities this account can use. Authorization is by this set — it never inherits a role. Delete and admin-level grants are allowed but flagged.
form.secretDescription: This is the only time the token is shown.

errors.invalidFields: Some fields are invalid. Check the values and try again.

rotate.secretDescription: This is the only time the new token is shown.
rotate.confirmDescription: A new token is minted for {name}. The current token stops working immediately — any system using it must be updated. The new token is shown once.

secretReveal.createdMessage: {name} was created. Here is its token.
secretReveal.rotatedMessage: {name} was rotated. Here is its token.
secretReveal.warning: Copy it now — you won't see it again. We only store a hash of the token, so it can never be shown or recovered later. If you lose it, rotate the account to mint a new one.
secretReveal.downloadTokenAria: Download token as a text file
secretReveal.acknowledge: I've saved this token in a secure place.

keypairSetup.done: Encryption key set up. This service account can now retrieve secrets from vaults you grant it access to.
keypairSetup.forbidden: You need Secret Manager manage permission to set up the encryption key. The service account is fine, but can't retrieve secrets until an admin sets it up (rotate its token).
keypairSetup.error: Couldn't set up the encryption key. The service account is fine — rotate its token to try again and enable programmatic secret retrieval.

testIt.title: Test it works
testIt.description: Run a quick check from your terminal to confirm the token authenticates and is scoped as expected. Replace the placeholder with the token you copied.
testIt.dialogDescription: Quick checks for “{name}”, based on the permissions it holds. The token is shown as a placeholder — paste in your own.
testIt.noChecks: This account holds no permission that maps to a representative check.
testIt.expect: Expect a {status} on success. Any 401/403 means the token is wrong, inactive, expired, or missing that permission.
testIt.hostNote: Host comes from your API URL. In dev, routes are bare (e.g. /assets). Behind the reverse proxy in production, the public path is /api/* (e.g. /api/assets).
testIt.openApiProd: The OpenAPI explorer is available only in development; it is not exposed publicly in production.

inventory.label: Inventory
inventory.description: Assets, consumables, models, categories and locations.

access.label: Access
access.description: Applications and who can access them.

knowledge.label: Knowledge
knowledge.description: The Knowledge Base — articles and their categories.

manage.label: Manage
manage.description: Users, instance settings, the dashboard and search.

automation.label: Automation
automation.description: The Applications Workflow Engine — workflow definitions, runs, manual tasks and connector credentials.

inventory:view.label: View inventory
inventory:view.description: See assets, consumables, models, categories and locations.

inventory:edit.label: Add & edit inventory
inventory:edit.description: Create and update assets, consumables, models, categories and locations (incl. stock adjustments).

inventory:delete.label: Delete inventory
inventory:delete.description: Archive assets, consumables, models, categories and locations.

inventory:import.label: Run bulk imports
inventory:import.description: Use the guided Migrator to bulk-import assets from a CSV/JSON file. Also requires the relevant write permissions (assets, models, categories, locations), checked per row at commit.

infra:view.label: View the server map
infra:view.description: See the infra topology canvas — nodes, edges and the per-node drill-in (owner, KB, IP, shortcuts).

infra:manage.label: Manage the server map
infra:manage.description: Create, edit and delete topology nodes, open and close edges, and persist node positions on the canvas. Asset-backed node creation also requires the asset edit permission.

accessGrant:view.label: See who has access
accessGrant:view.description: View the access-grant ledger — who can access which applications.

accessGrant:grant.label: Grant & revoke access
accessGrant:grant.description: Open, revoke and edit access grants for any user — including to sensitive applications. Also approve and deny access requests.

accessRequest:create.label: Request access
accessRequest:create.description: Ask for access to an application (with an optional level and justification). Approving or denying the request is the separate Grant & revoke access capability.

accessRequest:view.label: See access requests
accessRequest:view.description: View the estate-wide list of access requests (who asked for what). A requester can always see their own requests regardless of this.

article:edit.label: Write & edit articles
article:edit.description: Create, update and publish Knowledge Base articles.

article:manage.label: Edit any article
article:manage.description: Edit, publish, delete and restore ANY Knowledge Base article — not just your own. Still requires the write/delete capability for the action, and folder access is still respected.

user:view.label: View the user directory
user:view.description: Browse the list of users (names, emails, roles).

user:manage.label: Administer users
user:manage.description: Create, edit, change roles, offboard and restore users.

dashboardSearch:view.label: View dashboard & search
dashboardSearch:view.description: See the dashboard and use global search.

settings:view.label: View instance settings
settings:view.description: See the settings area (instance configuration, taxonomies).

settings:manage.label: Configure the instance
settings:manage.description: Change instance settings and manage taxonomies — the full admin configuration surface.

workflow:view.label: View workflows & runs
workflow:view.description: See workflow definitions, run history and the manual-task inbox.

workflow:manage.label: Configure workflows & connections
workflow:manage.description: Create, edit, enable and delete workflow definitions and their connections.

workflow:run.label: Run & retry workflows
workflow:run.description: Manually trigger, re-run and retry workflow runs.

workflow:task.label: Complete manual tasks
workflow:task.description: Action and complete manual task steps assigned to you (or your cohort).

workflow:secrets.label: Manage connector credentials
workflow:secrets.description: Configure, enter and rotate per-app connector credentials — kept separate from authoring the workflow logic.

notifications:view.label: View notifications
notifications:view.description: See the in-app notification bell — curated operational nudges (critical-app access, admin elevation, low stock, workflow tasks).

secret:view.label: View the Secret Manager
secret:view.description: See that vaults and secret items exist (names, handles, member lists) — zero-knowledge metadata only; no values are revealed.

secret:manage.label: Manage vaults & memberships
secret:manage.description: Create, edit and delete vaults; manage vault memberships (grant/revoke wrapped DEKs) — the full Secret Manager administration surface.

editor.label: Editor
editor.description: Read and edit everything except deletes and admin actions.

readOnly.label: Read-only
readOnly.description: View access across the app (no edits).

inventoryOperator.label: Inventory operator
inventoryOperator.description: Read and edit Inventory; view-only on Access, Knowledge and Manage.

taxonomies.title: Taxonomies
taxonomies.subtitle: Manage the categories that classify records, plus the asset models assets reference.

category.title: New {kind, select, asset {asset category} application {application category} consumable {consumable category} article {article category} other {category}}
category.description: Create a category to use it right away. You can refine it later.

model.title: New model
model.description: Create a make/model to use it right away. You can refine it later.

categories.emptyDescription: Add your first one to start classifying records — it becomes pickable wherever this kind is referenced.

bulkDelete.confirmTitle: Delete {count, plural, one {# category} other {# categories}}?
bulkDelete.confirmDescription: This soft-deletes the selected categories. Any that are still in use — they have articles or sub-folders — are kept and skipped.
bulkDelete.resultAllDeleted: Deleted {deleted, plural, one {# category} other {# categories}}.
bulkDelete.resultAllSkipped: {skipped, plural, one {# category} other {# categories}} skipped (still in use).

form.editDescription: Update the details of this category.
form.newDescription: Categories classify records across the app. Name is required; the rest are optional.
form.descriptionPlaceholder: Optional — what belongs in this category.
form.iconPlaceholder: Optional — a heroicon name, e.g. ServerStackIcon

specsDictionary.label: Specs dictionary
specsDictionary.description: Declare the custom fields assets in this category should have. Advisory only — it powers autocomplete and soft hints on the asset form; it never blocks a save or invalidates existing assets.

errors.invalid: Check the dictionary: every field needs a key and a label, choice-list fields need at least one value, and keys must be unique.

errors.orderInteger: Order must be a whole number.

models.emptyDescription: Add a make and model — say, a MacBook Pro 14 — so every asset you register can reference it instead of retyping the specs.

form.editDescription: Update this make/model and the defaults copied into new assets.
form.newDescription: A generic make/model that assets are instances of, e.g. “Dell Latitude 5520”.

defaultSpecs.label: Default specs
defaultSpecs.description: Fields copied into new assets that use this model. Each asset can still change them.
